shape.description: Red barrel body three cells long, shaped like a little truck: a threaded white or grey knob sticks out of the back end, a white dome closes the top at the middle, a rounded window opens in each side under the dome at the muzzle's level (the two entries), the front end is an open-top channel on the plunger axis (the exit). White arched leg caps at each end sit on the tops of two stacks with one empty cell between; the body rests on them.
shape.sizeBasis: Measured against the blue and orange blocks it stands on in uploads/M-28_1793563422019 (about 210 px a block width): about 4 block widths from nose to knob tip, nose 0.76 and back 0.69 cells past the leg centres, knob 0.3 cells, dome top 2.2 block widths over the blocks' tops. Grid scale (2026-11-07): one cell 45 mm, one slot 45.3 mm (B-01, src/catalog/parts.js). The earlier figure used a 52 mm cell and a 36 mm slot, which disagreed with this record's own ports and heightSlots.

accepts: top of a stack of the same height

physics.behaviour: Hand launcher, very strong. A marble rolls in through either side window and waits in the chamber on the plunger axis; a child pulls back the knob and the marble shoots out of the front along the plunger axis. Joey (2026-11-09): no turn within 5 to 7 cells of the exit or the marble flies out of the turn, and an up-ramp within about 3 cells. Nothing enters from above: the dome is closed. First piece of the line in Levels 1 and 2 (marbles go in by hand); mid-line in Level 3, where T-04 feeds a side window.

evidence.shows: Warnings: do not aim at eyes or face, do not discharge other objects: the set has a projectile launcher
Level 1: stands on L4 and N4 (both height 2), knob south; T-07 from front to M-10; no feed
Level 2: stands on N4 and N6 (both height 3), knob east; front into T-04, curving to M-10; no feed
Level 3: stands on J5 and L5 (both height 2), knob south; T-06 to M-10; T-04 arrives from the I7 side and enters the window under the dome
Real piece on plates: threaded knob, dome, window, open channel at front

evidence.source: vtechkids product text, via web search result only
evidence.shows: Dino-snack launcher; propel marbles into the jaws. Page could not be opened directly; treat as weak
Measured against the two blocks under it: about 180 mm long with the knob, 100 mm over the blocks, legs about 2 cells apart; sizeMm was 160 x 52 x 75 at a 52 mm cell
entries are the two side windows, exit along the plunger; it stands on the blue blocks; very strong: no turn within 5 to 7 cubes, a climb within about 3

assumptions: Port heights assume track level is one slot above the supports: M-10 base adds one slot on the same height stack, and the track between them is level in every placement.
Knob mechanism unknown: pull or push, spring assumed.
Hand loading in Levels 1 and 2 is assumed since nothing feeds it there; where the marble goes in is unconfirmed.
faces uses E=+x, W=-x, S=+y, N=-y, in the piece's own frame. Heights are slots above the floor when the piece stands on the floor or, where stated, above the top of its supports.
launchSpeed 2.5 m/s is assumed from Joey's 5 to 7 cube rule, not filmed.
Side windows take the same tracks a block side does (T-02, T-03, T-04, T-06, T-07); only T-04 is seen in a plan.

Side windows at z 1, the muzzle's track level (seat 0.68 slot over the stand tops): the window sill is the chamber floor, level with the muzzle channel (diagnosis 2026-11-09, Blender M-28.py sill). An earlier 0.85 named no level.
